title: Lambda event functions: small work with explicit retry boundaries
outcome: Choose an event-function boundary and handle retry, concurrency, and database pressure.
benefits: Managed event-driven compute without operating a VM per handler.
drawbacks: Trigger semantics, cold starts, concurrency, and downstream limits remain.
version: AWS SDK for Ruby v3 · service-specific setup · no cloud resources created automatically
cue: Small handler, explicit source contract, bounded downstream work.

trace.title: Configured source
trace.detail: This chapter focuses on Lambda event functions: a handler invoked under a configured event source. Other Lambda offerings have different contracts. A small S3 metadata check or queue-driven transformation can fit well; a large always-warm Rails web process is a different decision.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Source event → invocation/batch → validate record → durable effect → source-specific acknowledgement/failure handling. A retry may invoke the handler again with the same logical item.

Measure cold-start and dependency latency for the actual interaction. Bound concurrency so a surge does not create more database connections than RDS can support.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: Stateless compute does not mean the business effect is idempotent. Execution environments may be reused, so avoid treating mutable globals as per-user durable state.
